context: Pure refactor, no behaviour change. Move the async recovery into src/lib/compareRecovery.ts with an explicit result type distinguishing confirmed absence from transient load failure. Move planCompareIds alongside it for what it actually is - dedupe-and-cap - not as the recovery kernel. Compare keeps consuming both. Unit tests cover retained / missing / duplicate / over-limit / empty and the multi-stays-multi rule.
description:
Compare implements the only working stale-selection recovery in the product: it resolves short IDs, fetches details, partitions requested IDs into retained / missing / failed, reports 'These results may have been removed from the published dataset', canonicalises the URL to short IDs, and deliberately keeps a multi-selection URL multi after a one-result recovery so it does not collapse into the single-result builder (Compare.tsx:218-300, 331-350).

An earlier plan proposed extracting planCompareIds as the recovery kernel. That is wrong: planCompareIds (Compare.tsx:94-113) is a SYNCHRONOUS string helper - trim, dedupe, slice - with no database access. It cannot detect a missing run. All three reviewers caught this. The boundary worth extracting is the ASYNC recovery, and it is substantially larger.
